summary: preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: The package advertises itself as a trivial monorepo test package (lib/index.js exports the literal string 'John'), but its package.json declares a preinstall lifecycle script (`node setup.mjs`) that downloads the Bun runtime binary from GitHub releases, chmods it executable, and invokes it against a sibling file math_init.js at install time. setup.mjs is obfuscated with hex-name identifiers (`_0xNNNN`) and per-function string-scramble objects concealing URLs and command flags. math_init.js is a 727 KB heavily obfuscated blob using an obfuscator.io-style rotating string-array (`WV8StW` shuffle) whose contents are not human-readable and bear no relation to the package's stated purpose. The combination — obfuscated install-lifecycle code that fetches an alternate JavaScript runtime specifically to execute an obfuscated in-package payload — is a supply-chain dropper pattern that evades Node-based scanning by running the payload under Bun. Installing this package causes arbitrary attacker-controlled code to execute on the installer's machine via `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
